applicability.conditional: Applies only where the measured subject exists.

coverage: The share of countries meeting the expected reporting cadence during the latest five completed years.

glossary.definition: A comparison made after accounting for other named characteristics in the model.
A range obtained by repeatedly resampling countries and recalculating the result.
An indicator series that applies only where the measured subject exists.
A model-based range showing the uncertainty around an estimate.
One country evaluated for one indicator series.
The share of countries meeting an indicator's expected recent reporting cadence.
How rarely an indicator series is reported across countries.
One statistic tracked over time, such as maternal mortality or access to electricity.
A 0–100 ranking that combines staleness, missingness, global scarcity, and population.
The share of expected recent observations absent from the selected UN source.
The direct difference between two percentages; 50% minus 40% is 10 percentage points.
Recalculating a result under reasonable alternative choices to see whether it persists.
How overdue the latest observation is relative to its expected reporting cadence.
One of the UN's 17 shared development goals.
An indicator series intended to apply to every country.

measurement_priority.formula: 100 × weighted average of staleness, missingness, global scarcity, and population rank
measurement_priority.scale: 0 to 100; higher means a larger reporting gap under the chosen weights.
measurement_priority.scope: Only universal series receive a measurement-priority score.

weights.label: Staleness
weights.meaning: How overdue the latest observation is.

weights.label: Missingness
weights.meaning: How many expected recent reporting years are absent.

weights.label: Global scarcity
weights.meaning: How rarely the series is reported across countries.

weights.label: Population
weights.meaning: How large the affected population is, using log-population rank.

research.label: What is compared
research.text: Recent missingness, averaged equally across the same universal series for each country.

research.label: Adjusted comparisons
research.text: Country groups are compared descriptively; adjusted results account for region, income group, and log population as stated.

research.label: Intervals
research.text: Country-bootstrap intervals show stability to country composition. Model intervals use robust standard errors.

research.label: How to read the results
research.text: Associations describe this source and selection of series; they do not establish causes or measure all data a country collects.
